articles.title: Cody Bellinger's HR breaks open another Yankees win to eliminate Red Sox in lopsided wild-card series
articles.summary: An intentional walk of Ben Rice to face Cody Bellinger was just one of Boston's missteps in this series.
articles.body: The New York Yankees have advanced to the American League Division Series. Convincingly.For the second straight game, the club made its rivalry with the Boston Red Sox look far from competitive, winning Game 2 of their wild-card series 9-2 to finish off a sweep. The Yankees will face another AL East foe, the Tampa Bay Rays, in the next round.The Yankees did this without Aaron Judge, whose health still looms over the Bronx. Game 1 of the ALDS is scheduled for Saturday at 6:30 p.m. ET.Wednesday's wild-card Game 2 started as a duel between starting pitchers Max Fried and Sonny Gray but turned into a rout gradually and then suddenly. First came a Luis García Jr. homer to break a scoreless tie in the fourth inning. Cody Bellinger doubled the New York lead in the fifth with an RBI single, right after the Red Sox opted to pull Gray. Luis García Jr. and the Yankees strike first in Game 2! pic.twitter.com/2PgJzL6JfW— MLB (@MLB) October 1, 2026 Then came the sixth inning.It began hopefully for the Red Sox, who scored their first run of the series on a Willson Contreras homer that might or might not have received some help from a fan. Either way, Contreras and Fried exchanged hard stares during a long home run trot. Game on, right? Right?Boston's next lever to pull was bringing in ace Garrett Crochet for his first appearance since April, returning from shoulder inflammation and a lat strain. It was a nice story, one that was soon ruined by Crochet failing to get any of his four batters out. He exited with his team down by two runs, with the bases loaded and no outs.The Red Sox brought in setup man Garrett Whitlock to try to keep the game competitive, but productive outs scored two more runs. Boston then intentionally walked Ben Rice to set up a faceoff between Whitlock and Bellinger.Bellinger made that decision look foolish.Everything that followed was merely procedural for a lopsided Yankees win. The Red Sox made themselves a playoff team after a start so bad they fired manager Alex Cora, and they could do no wrong for one magical stretch in the middle of the season. However, there was once again a clear talent deficit against the Yankees, even without Judge.This is the second straight year that Boston has ended its season in New York, though the Sox at least played a Game 3 last season. This time around, they were outscored 18-2. The Yankees' two starting pitchers, Fried and presumptive Cy Young winner Cam Schlittler, combined to throw 12 1/3 innings with 5 hits and 1 run allowed, with 16 strikeouts.The Red Sox had injuries, of course, their most recent being Roman Anthony in Game 1. And it's not like we can pretend they had the fully functional version of Crochet. Still, this result begs the question of what the plan is under chief baseball officer Craig Breslow, who has appeared to steer the club into the exact kind of tier MLB teams want to avoid in the long term.Yankees fans haven't exactly been thrilled with their team's recent era, either, but they at least get to watch their team play this weekend, with the hope of benefiting from a chaotic American League field this season. New York gets two full days of rest before its series opener against the Rays, against whom they went 6-7 in the regular season.Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the New York Yankees host the Boston Red Sox in Game 2 of the AL wild-card round on Wednesday.

articles.title: Alec Bohm's 10th-inning homer, Andrew Painter's clutch relief deliver Phillies Game 2 wild-card win vs. Braves
articles.summary: Bohm went yard in extras, and Painter, making his postseason debut, came out of the bullpen to spin 3 scoreless innings.
articles.body: With free agency looming, Alec Bohm was struggling mightily during the first half of the 2026 campaign. Through June 17, he was slashing.227/.280/.369. That day was also when his Philadelphia Phillies optioned rookie starting pitcher Andrew Painter to Triple-A Lehigh Valley.More than three months later, Bohm and Painter saved the Phillies' season.Bohm hit a go-ahead solo home run in the 10th inning Wednesday in Game 2 of the National League wild-card series against the Atlanta Braves. He offered the Phillies a late lead they desperately needed after going down 3-1 in an elimination game, and Painter preserved it.Making his postseason debut — out of the bullpen, no less — Painter delivered three scoreless innings of relief.The 23-year-old righty sealed Philadelphia's 4-3 victory with a 99-mph four-seam fastball that clipped the inside edge of the zone and that ABS overturned for strike three to clinch a game-ending strikeout.The NL East champion Braves came into the afternoon riding high after Austin Riley's eighth-inning, three-run homer lifted them to a 5-3 victory in Game 1.At the onset of Game 2, Philadelphia's season rested in the palm of Cristopher Sánchez's left hand. The sterling southpaw, the runner-up for the NL Cy Young Award last year, took the mound. The Phillies needed his best stuff, especially considering their bullpen inconsistencies and that they tabbed closer Jhoan Duran for two innings in the series-opening defeat.As was the case in Game 1, the Phillies established a 1-0 advantage in the opening frame. Trea Turner led off with a double down the right-center alley. Bryce Harper drove him in, going the opposite way on a single to left. For reference, Braves right-hander Tyler Mahle had given up a combined one earned run in his two starts against the Phillies earlier this month.Mahle eventually settled in, though, and so did Sánchez after he conceded a first-inning run as well. Atlanta got on the board in part because of Ronald Acuña Jr.'s baserunning. After working a seven-pitch leadoff walk, he stole a pair of bags. The former NL MVP — who led the NL in stolen bases in 2019 and 2023 — swiped third with two outs and Matt Olson at the plate. Olson drove him home with a single to tie the game.Ronald Acuña Jr. makes an impact immediately 😤He successfully steals second AND third base, then comes around to score! pic.twitter.com/OtfgjQv3EZ— MLB (@MLB) September 30, 2026 After those two first-inning runs, it stayed 1-1 until the seventh.Sánchez dialed up 1-2-3 innings in the second and fourth. Following a 23-pitch first frame, he discovered a groove that came with improved efficiency. In the third, he caught Acuña looking at three straight strikes.When all was said and done, Sánchez went 6 2/3 with six strikeouts and three earned runs allowed. He recorded 116 pitches, eight more than he accounted for in any game in the regular season.As for Mahle, he logged six strikeouts in seven innings with just one run surrendered. His splitter proved spellbinding. The 32-year-old, whom the Braves acquired from the San Francisco Giants ahead of the trade deadline, deployed that pitch to punch out both Kyle Schwarber and Harper in the fifth inning.Things got hairy for Sánchez in the sixth. Atlanta had the bases loaded with one out. But Sánchez stayed composed and induced a ground ball toward first that led to a 3-2-3 double play. Bohm fired to home before scurrying to the first-base bag to make the inning-ending putout.3-2-3 DOUBLE PLAYThe Phillies escape the bases-loaded jam! pic.twitter.com/5lKM9tYRjr— MLB (@MLB) September 30, 2026 More trouble followed. In the seventh, with two men on, Drake Baldwin lifted a fly ball to right field that Harper badly misplayed. He didn't expect it to carry as far as it did and wound up leaping to try to make up for lost ground. But that was too little, too late, as the ball hit off Harper's glove. Baldwin was credited with an RBI double. The extra-base hit advanced Ha-Seong Kim to third, and an Olson sac fly plated Kim to put the Braves up 3-1. In the next half-inning, Harper instantly redeemed himself. After a 447-foot no-doubter from Schwarber quieted Truist Park in leading off. Then Harper also teed off on Mahle's replacement, lefty reliever Dylan Lee. Harper's solo shot traveled to a similar spot beyond the right-center wall but not quite as far, measuring 418 feet.Those back-to-back homers erased Philadelphia's two-run deficit and made it 3-3.BRYCE HARPERBACK-TO-BACKTHIS GAME IS TIED pic.twitter.com/fiIJdIM4oz— MLB (@MLB) September 30, 2026 Bohm's extra-inning, opposite-field dinger finally gave the Phillies back the lead — one they wouldn't relinquish.Follow along with Yahoo Sports for in-game updates, highlights and more from Game 2 of the National League wild-card series between the Braves and Phillies.

articles.title: Padres again dominate Cubs' MLB-best offense to finish sweep, will face Brewers in NLDS
articles.summary: The Padres have been the hottest team in baseball since early September.
articles.body: The Chicago Cubs led MLB in runs scored during the regular season, with 850. Their postseason total will end at one, courtesy of the San Diego Padres.For a second straight game, the Padres had little trouble on Wednesday against a lineup led off by presumptive National League MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong. They took Game 2 by a score of 4-1, finishing off a wild-card sweep in front of a raucous crowd at Petco Park.Between the regular season and the postseason, the Padres have now won 19 of their past 22 games. They outscored the Cubs 12-1 across their two wild-card games.GOT 'EM pic.twitter.com/reemRMs99v— San Diego Padres (@Padres) October 1, 2026 Their reward will be an NLDS matchup with the Milwaukee Brewers, a 103-win team that isn't exactly getting rewarded for being the top seed in the NL bracket. Game 1 is scheduled for 7:30 p.m. CT Saturday in Milwaukee.The lone run of the Cubs' postseason wound up coming on a Nico Hoerner RBI single in the fourth inning against Padres starter Nick Pivetta. That prompted San Diego to go to its vaunted bullpen, and the Cubs couldn't get any traction after that.The group of Bradgley Rodriguez, Jason Adam, Adrian Morejon and Mason Miller combined to throw 5 2/3 innings with 2 hits, 1 walk and 4 strikeouts. On the offensive side, the Padres took the lead with a rally in the second inning — which included the first career postseason RBI for 20-year-old Ethan Salas, the youngest catcher in postseason history — and added a cushion with a Gavin Sheets homer in the fourth.Volume up for Petco Park's reaction to Gavin Sheets' homer 🔊 pic.twitter.com/v144jC3WNb— MLB (@MLB) October 1, 2026 From the first inning of Game 1, the Padres had the Cubs on their back foot. They are a talented team that finally found momentum in the last month of the regular season — so much so that the dynamics of the postseason changed significantly in that span. The Brewers might be MLB's best team since March, record-wise, but San Diego is suddenly looking like a complete team playing with urgency. That turn of events has ended the Cubs' season more quickly than anyone might have expected. Chicago spent months in the NL's top wild-card spot, but it wound up being the Padres hosting the Cubs in a very loud stadium. It's an anticlimactic ending for a talented team, but that will happen in the playoffs.

articles.title: Phillies' Aaron Nola Reportedly Starting vs. Braves over Zack Wheeler For MLB Playoffs Series Finale
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Phillies will go into Thursday's winner-take-all Game 3 against the Atlanta Braves in the National League Wild Card series with Aaron Nola starting on the mound.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Phillies will go into Thursday's winner-take-all Game 3 against the Atlanta Braves in the National League Wild Card series with Aaron Nola starting on the mound.

Per The Athletic's Matt Gelb , Phillies interim manager Don Mattingly is going with Nola rather than using Zack Wheeler on short rest with a spot in the NLDS at stake.

The Braves will counter with lefty Ray Kerr as an opener.

As a result of their four-game losing streak last week that prevented them from clinching a playoff spot early, the Phillies had to use Wheeler on the final day of the regular season.

Wheeler allowed one run over six innings in a 7-3 win over the Tampa Bay Rays to help Philadelphia secure its postseason berth, but the situation left his status for the wild card round unclear.

Even though Wheeler won't get the start, Mattingly told reporters after Wednesday's 4-3 win to extend the series "it'll be pretty much all hands on deck" for Game 3.

The Phillies are fortunate to have a deep starting staff that allowed them to go with All-Stars Jesús Luzardo and Cristopher Sánchez in the first two games against Atlanta.

However, Game 3 left Mattingly with a decision between Nola or Wheeler. John Clark of NBC Sports Philadelphia noted Wheeler has never started a game in the regular season or playoffs on short rest.

Wheeler's only relief appearance in his MLB career was in Game 7 of the 2023 NLCS against the Arizona Diamondbacks. He tossed 1.2 scoreless innings in a 9-7 loss.

Nola will be pitching on regular rest after starting on Saturday against the Rays. He only made it through one inning, allowing three runs on four hits in a 12-1 loss.

While Nola's overall stat line this season doesn't look great with a 4.67 ERA, he did get better as the year went on. The right-hander had a 3.33 ERA in 14 starts after the All-Star break.

Nola made three starts against Atlanta this season with two coming in a five-day span from Sept. 6-11. He allowed three runs and struck out eight over 13.1 innings in those two outings last month.

The Phillies forced Game 3 against Atlanta thanks to Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper hitting back-to-back homers in the eighth to tie the score at three. Alec Bohm delivered the go-ahead solo homer in the top of the 10th.

Andrew Painter finished the game on the mound with three scoreless innings out of the bullpen.

Game 3 between the Phillies and Braves from Truist Park will be played at 8 p.m. ET on Thursday. The winner will advance to play the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLDS starting on Saturday.

articles.title: 2026 MLB Free Agents Rumors and Predictions for Tarik Skubal, Randy Arozarena & More
articles.summary: The baseball gods are preparing to ignite the burners for the 2026 iteration of the MLB hot stove.
articles.body:
The baseball gods are preparing to ignite the burners for the 2026 iteration of the MLB hot stove.

With playoff eliminations adding to the list of franchises already in offseason mode, a big chunk of the league's focus has shifted over to free agency.

It appears a more mysterious place than normal given the impending expiration of the current Collective Bargaining Agreement, but it's still where teams will go to target potential upgrades. No one knows exactly how things will play out, but our crystal ball has some hunches based on the latest rumor-mill rumblings.

Seiya Suzuki has spent all five of his MLB seasons with the Chicago Cubs. It's possible he'll spend his sixth elsewhere.

A reunion hardly feels impossible, but the Cubs have plenty on their offseason to-do list. Their pitching staff needs attention, and both of their corner outfielders, Suzuki and Ian Happ, are headed to free agency. Suzuki is worth bringing back, but it wouldn't be cheap. Not after he tallied 58 homers and 189 RBI over this season and last.

External suitors have taken note. Per The Athletic's Mitch Bannon , the Toronto Blue Jays "are expected to pursue...Suzuki." They certainly won't be alone in that effort.

Toronto could use more thump in its lineup, but so could other win-now teams. The Seattle Mariners, for instance, might need a Randy Arozarena replacement ( more on that in a minute ), and Suzuki could be a great get for that gig.

Prediction: Suzuki signs with the Seattle Mariners.

Nine-Figure Contract Incoming for Randy Arozarena?

Save for the possible labor stoppage, free agency could not be coming at a better time for Seattle Mariners outfielder Randy Arozarena. Not only is he coming off of a career campaign, he's also entering a market featuring few rivals for the No. 1 spot among free agent position players.

As for that career efffort, it was a pretty monstrous one. He scored an AL-best 113 home runs, posted his best OPS in a full season ( .865 ), launched the second-most homers of his career (26) and swiped his third-most steals (26). Altogether, he wound up with a 151 wRC+ , per FanGraphs, putting him behind only MVP favorites Yordan Alvarez and Pete Crow-Armstrong.

For Arozarena to post this kind of numbers in a contract year can only mean good things for his paycheck. Per Ryan Divish of the Seattle Times , "multiple MLB sources believe that Arozarena will get at minimum a four-year, $100 million deal. And most believe it will likely be five years of somewhere around $110 to $125 million."

A contract that rich and that long figures to come from someone other than the Mariners, which might work for Arozarena, since he reportedly "has always preferred to play on the East Coast," per Divish. With a number of big-spending East Coast clubs needing more oomph in their offense, Arozarena's list of potential landing spots is not a short one.

Prediction: Arozarena signs with the Atlanta Braves.

The following two things are somehow both true about this year's free agent crop: It features perhaps the most dominant pitcher in baseball, and it looks incredibly light on star power.

Tarik Skubal, who punctuated the past two seasons with AL Cy Young honors, is a certified superstar. He'd be the top-ranked ace in just about any free agent class he populated.

In this specific set, though, he might head, shoulders and a torso above the rest. As The Athletic's Will Sammon relayed, "multiple executives from different clubs...said that this free-agent class doesn't feature a no-doubt playoff starter outside of Skubal."

Teams in need of an ace, then, might feel as if Skubal is a must-have, which perhaps will drive his contract cost to record-setting heights. That could restrict his market to only baseball's biggest spenders, perhaps setting up a showdown between the New York Mets and his current club, the Los Angeles Dodgers.

Prediction: Skubal re-signs with the Dodgers.

articles.title: In 2001, Derek Jeter formed a bond with a 10-year-old girl who lost her father on 9/11; 25 years later, the Yankees legend reunited with her at Yankee Stadium
articles.summary: Derek Jeter's emotional reunion with Brielle Saracini at Yankee Stadium on the 25th anniversary of 9/11 celebrates their enduring bond, rooted in loss and support in the aftermath of tragedy.
articles.body: Derek Jeter and Brielle Saracini had an emotional reunion at Yankee Stadium on Sept. 11, 2026, as the New York Yankees commemorated the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 attacks. The meeting reunited the former Yankees captain with a woman he had met when she was a 10-year-old girl mourning the loss of her father, United Airlines Flight 175 captain Victor Saracini.Jeter and Saracini met just days after the attacks when Saracini wrote the Yankees shortstop about her father and her dream of meeting Jeter. The letter reached the baseball star, who invited Saracini and her family to Yankee Stadium. The reunion of former teammates, family members and fans 25 years later was held during a ceremony that linked that first meeting with a milestone anniversary in New York’s history.Derek Jeter and Brielle Saracini reunite at Yankee StadiumWhen her father, Victor Saracini, was killed in the September 11 attacks, Saracini was 10 years old. He was the pilot of United Airlines Flight 175, which was hijacked and flown into the South Tower of the World Trade Center. articles.title: Inside hilarious White Sox wild-card series celebration that produced Munetaka Murakami's latest viral moment
articles.summary: The South Siders won a playoff series for the first time since their World Series run in 2005, and they celebrated like it.
articles.body:
The celebratory bonanza in the visiting clubhouse Wednesday night at Houston 's Daikin Park could easily have been mistaken for a team reveling in a World Series victory.

Yet the paroxysm of Chicago White Sox joy was fitting, considering it took place in the very stadium they won it all against the Astros in 2005.

And that their American League wild-card sweep of the Astros 21 years later marked the franchise's first postseason series win since the Sox earned that ring. Chicago snapped the second-longest active drought in that department, per MLB.com's Sarah Langs.

Not only that, but its triumph signified just the second season since the club's World Series title in 1917 that the South Siders have won a playoff series.

The White Sox lost a franchise-worst 121 games two seasons ago. This season, according to Langs , they became the first major-league team to ever make the postseason after two straight 100-loss campaigns (and the Sox had three of those in a row from 2023-25). Now they'll be playing October baseball, in the ALDS.

An upstart team led by second-year manager Will Venable and a trio of All-Stars — first baseman Munetaka Murakami , third baseman Miguel Vargas and center fielder Tristan Peters — is this year's lovable playoff underdog.

The Sox were barking after their 7-3 series-clinching win in Houston on Wednesday . That was merely one of many memorable moments from the pandemonium that ensued following the final out.

Murakami, a breakout rookie from Japan who broke a Shohei Ohtani record in the infancy of his first major-league season , burst onto the scene in 2026, in part because of his 35 homers and in part due to his charisma.

He went viral again after the White Sox clinched their first playoff berth in five years with a Sept. 24 win over the Kansas City Royals .

At the time, when he was asked to rate that celebration's champagne popping from 1-10, he exclaimed, "100! No 10, 100!"

Then, when he was asked how many champagne bottles he had opened, he repeated that same number, "100."

In an interview with CHSN, the 26-year-old Murakami gave one hilarious response after another, including after he was asked what he learned from his first celebration of this ilk.

"No," Murakami said, shaking his head . "I'm drunk. Oh my God."

Later, in that interview as well as in one with NBC Sports , he called back to his "100" remark, showcasing his unbridled bliss following the playoff series victory.

Murakami told NBC Sports, "I'm drunk. Yesterday, maybe hungover."

When asked if he meant "tomorrow hungover," Murakami said, "Yes!" Then he continued, "No, not yesterday. Tomorrow. Sorry! I don't speak English!"

Sean Burke humorously clarifies that he does, in fact, have a family

White Sox right-handed pitcher Sean Burke gave a quote that made the rounds on social media in the lead-up to his Game 2 wild-card start against the Astros.

It went like this : "This is my life. No family, no girl, no kids. This is all I do."

Clearly, Burke was locked in. He delivered, throwing eight strikeouts in four innings. Granted he allowed three solo shots, but his offense offered plenty of run support.

Afterward, as the celebration trickled out onto the field from the clubhouse, he clarified that widely circulated quote.

"I love you, mom," Burke said. "Sorry if you were upset about that. The quote got kind of cut off. It was 'no family of my own.' I love my family."

He added, pointing: "They were all over here somewhere today, came out, always support me."

Mike Vasil : part reliever, part emcee, part motivational speaker

Chicago right-handed reliever Mike Vasil was the one conducting that CHSN interview with Burke.

Vasil is a man of several talents, apparently. Not only can he emcee, but he also has inspirational words in his arsenal.

"There's nothing like today, and there's nothing like tomorrow. Live in the present," Vasil shouted in a clubhouse interview with CHSN .

Before that, Vasil, the roommate of Chase Meidroth , took a playful jab at the second baseman, who hit an insurance-providing three-run homer in the sixth inning.

"Chase is probably talking about how good he is, and that's OK," Vasil said. "He's my roommate. He hit a big homer. But at the end of the day, remember, stay humble, kid. Life comes at you quick."

The White Sox are headed to Cleveland for the ALDS. They'll play a Guardians team that edged out Chicago for the AL Central crown.

"Well, what we're going to do, we're going to get on a plane, and we're going to head to Cleveland, Ohio," Vasil said.

He paused that thought to note: "Somebody's pouring alcohol down my pants."

Then Vasil picked back up where he left off: "And what we're going to do is we're going to show up, play White Sox baseball and we're going to kick some ass."

articles.title: Diamondbacks manager Torey Lovullo returns to team on 2-year deal, AP source says
articles.summary: The Arizona Diamondbacks are bringing back manager Torey Lovullo on a two-year contract, a person with direct knowledge of the deal said Thursday.  The Arizo...
articles.body:
PHOENIX (AP) — The Arizona Diamondbacks are bringing back manager Torey Lovullo on a two-year contract, a person with direct knowledge of the deal said Thursday.

The person spoke to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity because the new deal hasn't been announced. The Arizona Republic first reported Lovullo's new deal.

The 61-year-old's future with the club was in flux after the D-backs missed the playoffs for a third straight year . Arizona was eliminated from postseason contention on the final day of the regular season for the second time in three seasons when the Phillies beat the Rays 7-4 on Sunday.

The D-backs finished with an 86-76 record — the best in MLB for a team that didn't qualify for October baseball.

Lovullo is the winningest manager in Diamondbacks history, going 750-768 during a full decade in charge, with the highlight being a surprise World Series appearance in 2023. He is the third-longest tenured manager in the big leagues behind Tampa Bay's Kevin Cash and Los Angeles Dodgers skipper Dave Roberts.

The affable Lovullo is a popular presence in the organization. He played eight seasons in the big leagues for seven teams in the 1980s and 1990s. He was the bench coach for the Boston Red Sox when they won the World Series in 2013 and played college baseball at UCLA.

articles.title: Diamondbacks reportedly give manager Torey Lovullo a two-year extension after team fell just short of playoffs
articles.summary: The Diamondbacks were eliminated from the playoffs on the final day of the regular season.
articles.body:
After being mired around .500 for the first half of the season, the Arizona Diamondbacks made a surprising postseason run in the second half, falling just short of the playoffs on the final day of the regular season.

Even though the team ultimately failed, its second-half surge was reportedly enough to get manager Torey Lovullo an extension, per the Arizona Republic's Nick Piecoro.

The deal is said to be for two years, per Piecoro, which puts Lovullo on the same contract timeline as team general manager Mike Hazen.

The move comes after an eventful season with Lovullo at the helm. While the Diamondbacks never truly struggled, the team went 49-47 in the first half. That was solid, but not good enough for a playoff spot. At the time of the All-Star break, the Diamondbacks sat 2.5 games back of the final wild-card position in the National League.

With the team still battling for the playoff spot a month later, star second baseman Ketel Marte failed to show up for a game against the Boston Red Sox . He was eventually placed on the restricted list and missed time due to a knee injury. During Marte's absence, Lovullo faced multiple questions about the second baseman's behavior and how the team would handle it.

Marte eventually returned and — to Lovullo's credit — the team rallied to finish the year. After a 15-10 July, the team went 15-14 in August. But through the first 15 games in September, the D-Backs were just 7-8 and saw their playoff chances slipping away.

On Sept. 18, the team sat five games out of a wild-card spot after losing their previous three contests. Their season appeared to be all but done.

But a six-game winning streak pushed the team to just a game back of the Philadelphia Phillies with two games to go. Both teams lost the next day, taking the playoff race to the final game of the season.

Though they fought valiantly at the end, the Diamondbacks couldn't get it done. The team lost its regular-season finale and the Phillies won. Arizona wound up missing the playoffs by two games.

The team's moderate start, combined with the Marte situation, led some to wonder whether Lovullo would be fired at the end of the regular season, even with the team's last-second surge. Instead, the Diamondbacks will show faith in their skipper, who has posted a .494 winning percentage in his 10 seasons with the franchise.

He won't have long to prove the team right. The two-year deal sends a clear message to both Hazen and Lovullo. If the team doesn't bounce back and go on a deep playoff run in the next two years, both men are likely to be ousted at the same time, clearing the path for a new era in Arizona.

articles.title: Aaron Judge ruled out for the Yankees’ AL Wild Card Series
articles.summary: Aaron Judge is out for the Yankees’ AL Wild Card Series with a calf strain as New York turns to its depth against the Red Sox.
articles.body:
Aaron Judge is officially out of the Yankees' American League Wild Card Series against the Boston Red Sox. New York left its captain off the 26-man postseason roster after his right calf strain prevented him from proving he was ready for game action. Judge had pushed hard to return, including taking live batting practice before the roster deadline.

The decision came after several days of uncertainty about his availability, with Judge still trying to argue that he could help. New York entered the series as the AL's No. 4 seed after finishing 93-68. The Yankees then opened the postseason with a 9-0 win over Boston on Tuesday night. Judge's absence remains one of the defining storylines around the series.

Judge is recovering from a moderate strain of the soleus muscle in his right calf. The Yankees placed him on the injured list Sept. 19, retroactive to Sept. 17, after he was injured during the club's series against the Minnesota Twins. MLB reported that a moderate calf strain typically requires at least three weeks to fully heal.

The timing made the decision especially difficult. Judge returned from a long absence caused by a fractured right rib earlier in September, only to suffer another injury after appearing in seven games. He went 4-for-23 with one home run after returning, while his full 2026 season ended with a .241/.360/.511 slash line, 18 homers, and 41 RBIs in 66 games.

Judge did everything possible to make the roster conversation complicated. He told MLB that he had been "doing a lot of convincing" as he tried to show the Yankees he could contribute, and he participated in live batting practice shortly before the roster was finalized. Despite that progress, the club determined he wasn't ready for postseason game action.

The Yankees have already adjusted without their captain

New York has spent much of the season learning how to construct its lineup without Judge. His fractured rib kept him out for most of the summer, and the Yankees still secured a postseason berth before his calf injury ended his regular-season comeback. Manager Aaron Boone previously acknowledged that the club had performed reasonably well without its best player while maintaining the expectation of winning.

That depth was visible immediately in Game 1. Cam Schlittler delivered 6 1/3 scoreless innings with 10 strikeouts, while Ben Rice drove in six runs and hit a grand slam as New York defeated Boston 9-0.

Giancarlo Stanton also gives New York another experienced power option. Stanton was activated from the 60-day injured list and placed on the Wild Card roster after taking live batting practice Monday, although he entered the series as a potential pinch-hitting option rather than a regular starter. Trent Grisham was also activated and included on the 26-man roster.

Judge's absence still changes the Yankees' offensive ceiling

Even with the Game 1 rout, Judge's presence was difficult to replace. His career production has made him a central part of the Yankees' offensive identity, and his power can alter how opposing pitchers attack the lineup.

Judge has repeatedly produced at historic power levels. His 2022 season ended with 62 home runs, breaking Roger Maris' American League record, and he has multiple 50-homer seasons on one of the most prolific power résumés in Yankees history.

The difference was especially notable because the Wild Card Series was a short, best-of-three matchup. New York still absorbed Judge's absence, sweeping Boston in 2 games while scoring 18 runs across the series.

Fun fact: Aaron Judge became the fastest player in MLB history to reach 60 career home runs in terms of games played when he hit his 60th in his 197th game in April 2018.

What Judge's absence means for New York's lineup

Judge's absence removes one of the Yankees' biggest middle-of-the-order threats from the Wild Card Series. His combination of power, plate discipline, and postseason experience normally gives New York another layer in a lineup built around producing extra-base hits.

The Yankees have already shown that their offense can compensate through other contributors. Ben Rice's six-RBI performance in Game 1 provided the biggest example, while the club also received production from several spots in the lineup during its dominant victory over Boston.

The situation also puts greater importance on the Yankees' pitching staff. Cam Schlittler's 10-strikeout performance kept Boston from generating pressure, giving New York a path to win even without its captain available.

The Wild Card decision could affect the next round

Judge's exclusion from the Wild Card roster does not automatically end his postseason hopes. MLB reported that he would continue his rehabilitation with the possibility of returning for the American League Division Series, provided his calf progresses enough for the Yankees to clear him.

The Yankees finished the regular season 93-68 and earned the No. 4 seed, setting up a home Wild Card matchup with the No. 5 Red Sox. The series began Tuesday at Yankee Stadium, with both teams entering the postseason after navigating significant injury questions.

The Yankees advanced without Judge by sweeping Boston in 2 games. Schlittler's Game 1 performance, Rice's 6-RBI night, and a scoreless pitching effort from the bullpen helped New York take the opener, and the Yankees finished the series with a 9-2 win in Game 2.

Aaron Judge was left off the Yankees' 26-man AL Wild Card roster because of his right calf strain.

Judge played only 66 games in 2026 after also missing significant time with a fractured rib.

New York opened the series with a 9-0 win over Boston behind Cam Schlittler and Ben Rice.

The Yankees swept Boston in 2 games and advanced to face the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS.

Giancarlo Stanton and Trent Grisham were added to the postseason roster.

Judge could remain a postseason option if his calf heals sufficiently for the ALDS.

articles.title: Swing-and-a-miss: MLB rescinds idea to host baseball game in national park after backlash
articles.summary: Officials in Wyoming had called notion to host game in Grand Teton national park ‘deeply unwelcome’
articles.body:
Major League Baseball (MLB) leadership is no longer considering holding a game inside a national park, according to a letter commissioner Robert Manfred sent to officials in Teton county, Wyoming, on Thursday in what could be the league's biggest swing-and-a-miss off the diamond.

On 26 September, the Washington Post reported that MLB had reached out to the White House about staging a one-day game at Grand Teton national park in Wyoming . Teton county describes itself as a "a year-round resort community" and sits within the Jackson Hole valley. It's also a habitat for grizzly bears, osprey, bison and more.

News of MLB's outreach to the federal government quickly sparked concern about the impact that erecting a field and the infrastructure to hold spectators could have on the natural landscape and habitat of scores of wildlife that call the 310,000-acre (125,500-hectare) park home.

In the letter, Manfred noted that MLB had held games at places like the Fort Bragg military base in North Carolina and the nation's oldest Negro Leagues stadium in Birmingham, Alabama. He added that MLB staff had been doing their due diligence to see whether a game at Grand Teton was possible and to evaluate the potential environmental impact.

"Since the story was reported, it has become clear that the local community does not want us to continue Grand Teton national park as a potential site," Manfred wrote.

The outrage over the possible MLB game comes as national parks across the US struggle under funding cuts, staffing shortages and consistent overcrowding.

A Teton county commissioner, Luther Propst, who described the potential game as an "incomprehensible and deeply unwelcome notion", celebrated the MLB's decision in a post on Facebook.

"Ever since I got a call from the Washington Post about [MLB] scouting a ballfield in Grand Teton National Park, I have been hoping this idea would die a quick death – and today it did!" he wrote. "This is what can happen when we stand up firmly together, and I am proud to have played my part."

In a statement to the Guardian, a White House spokesperson said that it was approached by the MLB about the possibility of hosting the game but the National Park Service had not granted any permits to do so and the game is not a White House directive.

Neither MLB nor the National Park Service immediately responded to the Guardian's request for comment.

Los Angeles was the better team in the regular season, and it comes into the NLDS with the far superior pitching rotation.

Atlanta has a strong ace in Chris Sale, but he won't be available on regular rest until Game 2.

That means the Braves need a combination of strong outings from their depth pitchers and a few big offensive performances to counter whatever the Dodgers throw at them during the best-of-five series.

Money Line: Los Angeles (-210; bet $210 to win $100); Atlanta (+176; bet $100 to win $176)

The Dodgers carry an overwhelming starting pitching advantage in the matchup with the Braves.

Tarik Skubal and Yoshinobu Yamamoto will likely start Games 1 and 2. Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow are available after them to make starts.

The postseason is where the Dodgers' pitching depth needs to shine more. It'll be hard for any team remaining in the playoff bracket to match their star power.

Skubal was acquired specifically to bolster the postseason pitching depth. Yamamoto was the 2025 World Series Most Valuable Player.

Los Angeles will be expected to get out to a series lead on home soil behind Skubal and Yamamoto.

The only comparable pitcher on the Braves roster to the Dodgers' top arms is Chris Sale, who would be in line to start Game 2 on Sunday night.

Sale could be in line to start Game 5 as well, if the series gets to that point, but Atlanta is going to have to piece things together far more than the Dodgers.

The goal for the Dodgers has to be to finish off the series in three, if not four, games because of its edge on the mound.

If the Dodgers somehow leave it to chance in Game 5, the advantage may go away because of a second Sale start.

Atlanta Needs to Carry Over Offensive Momentum

Atlanta isn't out of the series just because Los Angeles carries a slew of dominant arms.

The Braves come into the NLDS with some offensive momentum after they hit three home runs in the wild-card series-clinching Game 3.

Atlanta scored 14 runs against the Phillies, who put Cristopher Sanchez, Jesus Luzardo, Aaron Nola and Zack Wheeler out on the mound in the series.

The NL East champion scored 11 runs off the Dodgers in its three-game sweep on home soil at the end of August. Four of those runs came off Yamamoto and Glasnow.

The star-studded lineup, led by Ronald Acuna Jr. and Matt Olson, will carry the momentum from the wild-card round and the confidence from the August series into Dodger Stadium.

It certainly won't be an easy task to beat the Dodgers three times, but if the Braves do so, their offense will have played a big role in getting there.

articles.title: Braves hit 3 homers to beat Phillies 6-2 in wild card clincher
articles.summary: Atlanta will advance to a best-of-five Division Series against the two-time defending World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers.
articles.body: Michael Harris II hit a three-run homer in the first inning, Ray Kerr threw 3 1/3 scoreless innings and the Atlanta Braves beat the Philadelphia Phillies 6-2 on Thursday night in the decisive Game 3 of their National League Wild Card Series. Ozzie Albies hit a two-run homer in the fourth and Matt Olson added a solo shot in the seventh for the Braves, who advance to a best-of-five Division Series against the two-time defending World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers. The Braves won a postseason series for the first time since winning the 2021 World Series and earned their first playoff series win against the Phillies. Philadelphia beat Atlanta in the 1993 NLCS and the 2022 and 2023 NLDS. Phillies right-hander Aaron Nola was pulled after allowing three runs in 1 2/3 innings. Nola walked Ronald Acuña Jr. and Matt Olson with one out in the first before giving up the homer to Harris, who hit into two double plays in Wednesday’s 4-3 loss in 10 innings, which forced Thursday night’s game. Kerr made his postseason debut in only his fourth career start. Braves manager Walt Weiss wanted a left-hander to face Phillies left-handed hitters Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper at least once. Kerr allowed only one hit — to Schwarber in the first — and one walk — to Schwarber in the fourth. Right-hander Grant Holmes followed Kerr and allowed one run in two innings to earn the win. Kerr left to a standing ovation from the sellout crowd and acknowledged the cheers by lifting up his arm as he approached the dugout. Left-hander Chris Sale, the starter in Atlanta’s 5-3 win in Tuesday’s series opener, struck out Harper to end the eighth and closed out the win in the ninth by striking out Bryan De La Cruz and pinch-hitter Otto Kemp. Phillies right-hander Zack Wheeler, the winning pitcher in Sunday’s 7-3 victory over Tampa Bay that clinched the wild-card spot, walked Austin Riley in the fourth before giving up Albies’ homer to right field that gave Atlanta a 5-0 lead. Wheeler allowed two runs in four innings. Jonathan Bowlan, Philadelphia’s fourth pitcher, gave up Olson’s homer to center field. Kerr, 32, flourished in the postseason spotlight. He pitched in only nine games after being recalled by Atlanta on Aug. 16. He underwent Tommy John surgery in 2024 and didn’t pitch in 2025. Philadelphia’s 2022 World Series loss to Houston began a streak of five straight postseason appearances with progressively quicker exits — the NL Championship Series, two NLDS exits and now the wild-card loss.

articles.title: Bryce Harper Talks Future After Playoff Elimination, Phillies 'Will Look a Lot Different' in 2027
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Phillies' season ended in the American League Wild Card round on Thursday after a 6-2 loss to the Atlanta Braves.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Phillies' season ended in the American League Wild Card round on Thursday after a 6-2 loss to the Atlanta Braves.

The Phillies have plenty of questions heading into the offseason, and Bryce Harper expects the team to "look a lot different" in 2027.

"Each year's so different than the year before. I don't really put stock into years before or what happened or anything else," Harper said. "This was a brand new team. Obviously, we had the guys that are part of that core group that we are. I'd imagine this team is going to look a lot different next year with the guys that are leaving this clubhouse. So, we'll see."

Harper is tied to the Phillies through the 2031 season, so he'll remain in Philadelphia for years to come, barring a trade. Stars like Zack Wheeler, Kyle Schwarber, Trea Turner and Aaron Nola are also set to return.

But the Phillies have a handful of notable free agents , such as Alec Bohm, Jose Alvarado, Luis Arreaz, Emundo Sosa and more.

Perhaps the biggest question mark is who will be the Phillies' skipper in 2027.

Philadelphia fired manager Rob Thomson in April after a rough start to the season, and interim manager Don Mattingly helped the Phillies get back on track to reach the postseason, but he has yet to shed the interim tag.

Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic reported this week that Mattingly was "likely to be replaced" if the Phillies didn't make a deep run in the postseason, so it seems Philadelphia will be on the hunt for a new manager.

Schwarber spoke highly of Mattingly after the season ended on Thursday.

"Even when things got hard, the way that he was able to keep things at even-keel pace for us. I think that was huge," Schwarber said.

The Phillies were interested in Alex Cora after he was fired by the Boston Red Sox, but he turned the offer down. Cora said in April that he's interested in getting back into baseball at some point, but didn't clarify how soon that would be.

Even with an offseason full of changes coming, the Phillies will retain most of their core as they try to get back to the World Series. How different the team will look in the spring remains to be seen.

articles.title: Red Sox's Sonny Gray Was Correct About Incredible Stats Third Time Through Lineup
articles.summary: The right-hander was excellent.
articles.body:
Postseason moves are always tough to decide on in Major League Baseball, something the Boston Red Sox could be thinking about after Wednesday night's game against the New York Yankees.

The Red Sox decided to take out Sonny Gray after 4.2 innings. He allowed six hits and two earned runs.

It would have been Gray's third time through the lineup, and in typical postseason fashion, skippers usually pull guys. Manager Chad Tracy decided to do just that, but it wasn't popular with some in the clubhouse.

Regarding how Gray felt, he said after the game that he was the best pitcher in Major League Baseball the third time through the lineup.

"I'm the best pitcher in the American League third time through the order. I think that's a fact. I would have liked to have been trusted in that moment."

According to CBS Sports, Gray's comment was factual, as he was the best starter in the American League the third time through the order. He posted a 1.99 ERA in 45.1 innings this season.

"Gray was spot-on. He, indeed, was the best starter in the American League the third time through the order, carrying a 1.99 ERA in 45 ⅓ innings pitched, a large enough sample size," CBS wrote .

While Gray was able to do some very impressive things during the regular season three times through a lineup, the postseason brings different challenges.

Factor that in with him already allowing two earned runs, and the Red Sox decided to go in a different direction.

Ultimately, the team only scored two runs, and while things might have been different, there's no telling now.

articles.title: What stories of MLB postseason heroes teach us about low-cost youth sports
articles.summary: Michael Harris II (Braves) and Braden Montgomery (White Sox) are among the MLB Develops alumni shining in the playoffs.
articles.body:
As parents of athletes, we learn to be strategic (and realistic) about how to move our son or daughter along the line. Maybe we played sports at some level and can offer guidance.

Del Matthews went into parenting with experience in big league clubhouses. His father, Gary "Sarge" Matthews , was a standout major leaguer who played 16 years, while his brother, Gary Jr., was also an All-Star outfielder who lasted 12 in the majors.

Del, who played in college and the minor leagues, understands how sports experiences can set up your life without you "making it." He and his brothers played Little League , too.

"I fell in love with the game early," he tells USA TODAY Sports, "and, really, it was being at the ballpark with my dad and watching him interact with his teammates and watching him win and compete and just emulating what I grew up watching and the conversations that I was hearing, and acting that out with my brothers when we went to the park."

Del Matthews is now Major League Baseball's senior vice president of baseball development as part of MLB's initiatives that include cost-free events and showcases and youth academies in a growing number of U.S. cities to increase baseball and softball accessibility.

Twelve players competing in this year's postseason are a product of MLB Develops programming , which Matthews helps oversee. He has known many of them since they were 13 or 14.

"So many things in the (youth) space are tournament based, and pay-for-play , showcase based," Matthews says, "and so what we try to do is take away the pay barrier for some of these opportunities, but also give kids skill development and things that are going to help them.

"And so whether they go back and play for their high school team or their travel team, they're really equipped with the necessary skills that are going to sustain them through high school, make them better players and hopefully ready to compete at the next level."

When he says "the next level," Matthews, 49, doesn't necessarily mean being in the same room with future Hall of Famers some day, the way his dad was.

He shared perspective on what MLB teaches about trying to get as far as you can in the game, and how that journey can be worthwhile no matter how far you reach.

MLB Develops is a network of baseball and softball intersquad games, showcases and other events aimed at kids through the high school level. Matthews, under former Angels general manager Tony Reagins , has helped reshape MLB youth initiatives over the past decade with more of a development mindset.

They start with grassroots events for younger kids like Play Ball and Pitch Hit & Run . They rise through an MLB ID tour in 18 to 20 cities from eighth grade to high school. GRIT is the same as the ID tour for girls baseball.

Players are identified at ID tour events and invited to larger summer showcases such as the three-day Breakthrough Series and five-day Hank Aaron Invitational . There is also the DREAM Series in January.

There's the Trailblazer Series for girls baseball and Jennie Finch Classic for softball, as well as a Breakthrough Series and Elite Development Invitational for each.

The majority of these events are done in conjunction with USA Baseball. The women's space can be a pipeline to the women's national baseball team and softball team .

Who are the MLB Develops alumni in the 2026 postseason?

When the postseason began, program alumni included infielders Travis Bazzana (Guardians), David Hamilton (Brewers) and George Lombard (Yankees); outfielders Justin Crawford (Phillies), Michael Harris II (Braves), Brice Matthews (Astros), Braden Montgomery ( White Sox ), Chandler Simpson (Rays), Cam Smith (Astros), Taylor Trammell (Astros); DH Dominic Smith (Braves); and pitcher Carlos Rodón (Yankees).

Matthews (from Houston) and Smith (Compton, California) came out of two of the nine youth academies MLB runs in urban communities, which have provided more than 10 major league players. Other youth academies are located in New Orleans, Cincinnati, Philadelphia, Dallas, Kansas City (Missouri), Miami, and Washington, D.C.

2026 MLB playoffs open with thrilling wild-card series matchups

The academies are free and open to everyone, typically for grade school through high school kids who live in those communities. They can be a starting ground for players getting recommended for the development events. Kids go through drills and group style workouts but also come in after school for educational and vocational programming, such as SAT prep and broadcasting.

The youth academies gather every All-Star Week to compete in the Commissioner's Cup (baseball) and Jennie Finch Classic (softball), but the focus is on the everyday aspect of what a commitment to a sport can bring you and what it takes to keep advancing.

"For some kids that don't get selected, what we try to advise is, pick one or two showcases that you want to go to," Del Matthews says. "You don't have to go to every showcase. You don't have to compete in every single tournament. A lot of parents have the fear of missing out that if maybe another kid on the team was (here) that they missed their opportunity. And that is not really the case. Everybody's development arc is a little bit different and so pick one or two showcases or tournaments you can afford.

"The most important thing is getting an opportunity (on a team) where you can play . … We try to instill the message you want to be ready for the showcase when you go there and pay for it, not just pay for an evaluation. You want to make sure that you have the requisite skills that you're actually ready for it, and that you've shown growth, you've shown improvement, and that you're going to be invited back based upon your skill level and not just the monetary value that the entity is getting from it."

'You don't have to go to every tournament': What do stories of MLB Develops alumni teach us about the youth sports pipeline?

Harris, the Braves' 25-year-old starting center fielder in the wild card series , went 3-for-3 with two runs scored in the Braves' 5-3 Game 1 win over the Phillies. He hit a three-run homer in their decisive Game 3 win .

As a kid growing up in the Atlanta area, he liked to pick flowers in the outfield. In one game, his father remembered for an MLB documentary , he was distracted by the activity and wouldn't go after the ball.

He played a number of sports as a kid and his mentality changed about baseball as he got bigger, faster and stronger.

He played in MLB's Reviving Baseball in Inner Cities (RBI) program, which provides resources and support for underserved communities . He met former Braves star Marquis Grissom , who runs a baseball academy , when he was about 14.

Scouts came out to watch someone playing against Harris and noticed him.

"He actually was a two-way player and was probably a little further along as a pitcher than he was as a hitter," Del Matthews says, "but he was a standout from the jump and had a chance to play on some of our tournament teams."

Dana Brown, then the Braves' vice president of scouting, saw Harris through MLB's Hank Aaron Invitational. The Braves drafted him in the third round in 2019. He has been in the majors since 2022.

Justin Crawford had more of a pedigree as the son of a four-time major league All-Star (Carl Crawford) but Matthews says he was small and wiry and behind some of the other players when he showed up to the MLB camp. He was motivated to put in more work when he went home to Las Vegas.

"He continued to do drills and practiced some of the things that he had learned in the summer when he would go home in the offseason," Matthews says. "He would just continue to get better and by the time he became a senior, really worked himself into one of the top players in the country and ended up going in the first round in the draft ."

What do the stories of MLB Develops alumni teach all youth athletes?

We tend to regard major leaguers as specimens born with generational talent. In many cases, they are, but how do they develop their talent?

Academic and psychologist Angela Duckworth closely studied perseverance in her acclaimed book, "Grit." She argues that while talent is important to achieving success in whatever you undertake, major drivers for achievement are tenacity and repetition of effort.

She puts herself in that category, relaying how her father used to tell her as a kid, "You're no genius."

Based on her research and conversations with success stories from sports, the military, business and elsewhere, she came up with a two-part formula for achievement: talent X effort = skill and skill X effort = achievement.

In other words, grit is crucial to success. And, she writes, where there's no joy, there's no grit. Think of Harris.

"When he stopped loving the game, I'd stop pushing him," his father, Michael Sr., said in the documentary, "but he never stopped."

We often settle on what we do in sports, school and life because it's our passion.

"If you love the game, our message is, 'Hey, just keep playing, keep getting better, find an opportunity (in or out of MLB programming) where you can play summer ball, where you can get at-bats, where you can get innings, where you can develop your skills," Matthews says. "And if you work hard, put in the repetition, good things will happen. It doesn't happen overnight but with baseball the long game is important and if you can enhance your skills over weeks, months and years, you have the best opportunity to continue to get better."

If there's something that interests you besides sports, do as much of it as you can to deepen your profile. Montgomery, who went 2-for-4 in Game 1 of the White Sox's two-game wild card sweep of the Astros, was a high achiever in academics who played at Stanford and Texas A&M.

"He was a great hitter at a very young age, very polished, but more impressive off the field, just well spoken, a great student," Matthews says. "I think he got a perfect score on his ACT as a sophomore

"Everybody wants to focus on the physical development, but really the academics is what gives you the options (and) opens doors. We emphasize that while you're away playing, if you're gonna be a collegiate athlete, you have to be able to balance being an athlete, but also making sure that you get your work done."

How can kids get involved in MLB Develops programming?

Check out a youth academy or come out to get a free evaluation at an ID Tour event. They start early in the year and run through April or early May.

MLB Develops events had nearly 2,200 players competing in 2026, with some overlap. Many more kids are impacted through MLB's grassroots events.

The players for the MLB Develops free events for high schoolers are hand-selected or come recommended. Some kids, Matthews says, will blindly email, send video or have an endorsement from a coach.

The competition for spots is stiff but carries an underlying message that Duckworth, the psychologist and author, can appreciate.

"I think your skills have to take care of themselves, but if you're not selected to participate, keep trying," Matthews says. "That's really what it's about. Any sport that you play you have to continue to get better and stronger and practice your skills."

As you work toward a goal, you might end up somewhere you didn't expect.

Matthews has three sons who have played baseball, and one of them, after playing the sport in high school, developed a passion for the culinary arts.

After those early days in big league clubhouses, and later playing at Texas Southern and in the Milwaukee Brewers organization , his father went back for more secondary education and into a front office career with the White Sox and MLB.

He will tell you what you do with your love of something can benefit a person deeply.

"Everybody's not gonna play at the highest levels ," Matthews says. "Everybody's not gonna get selected to all-star teams, but if you can have a great experience around the game, if you get a chance to go to a showcase and you make friends for a lifetime, that's really what it's about. It's about going to the ballpark and not knowing what you're gonna (see) and potentially something magical happening that day or rooting for your hometown team and having memorable lifetime experiences with your family ."

Steve Borelli, aka Coach Steve, has been an editor and writer with USA TODAY since 1999. He played baseball in high school, rowed in college and spent 10 years coaching his two sons' baseball and basketball teams. He and his wife, Colleen, are now sports parents to a college and high school baseball player. For his past columns, click here .

articles.title: Braves' unlikely duo of ace Chris Sale and newest folk hero Ray Kerr combine to seal wild-card win over Phillies, deliver Atlanta to the NLDS
articles.summary: Two unconventional pitching strategies worked perfectly for Atlanta in Game 3.
articles.body:
ATLANTA — In an all-or-nothing, loser-exits-the-season playoff game, starting a pitcher with all of 18 ⅓ innings pitched on the year is definitely one strategy. Bringing in your 200-strikeout ace, who threw 95 pitches just two days ago, to cover the critical final outs of the game is also a strategy. Fortunately for the Atlanta Braves, neither of these unconventional strategies blew up in manager Walt Weiss' face on Thursday, and as a result, Atlanta is now on the way to the NLDS to face Los Angeles .

In a bit of full-circle harmony, the Braves' most experienced pitcher and one of its least experienced came together to hold the line for Atlanta against the Phillies in a 6-2 victory . Ray Kerr started the no-tomorrow game, and if you have no idea who that is, you're not alone . Chris Sale finished the game, and if you don't know his whole story, well, you can visit his plaque in Cooperstown in a few years.

"Hopefully Ray Kerr became a bit of a household name tonight," Weiss said after the game. "He deserves it. He's got an amazing story."

Kerr's backstory went from cute anecdote to folk legend in the time it took him to throw 3 ⅓ scoreless innings against the Phillies, his longest — and, obviously, most critical — outing of the year. Now 32, he grew up in Reno, Nevada, one of six children, falling in love with fishing and bouncing in and out of foster care. He worked at a 7-Eleven and a movie theater before enrolling at Lassen Community College in California. He pitched well enough there and in the Alaska Baseball League that the Mariners and Marlins showed interest, and the Mariners offered him a minor-league slot and a $2,000 signing bonus in 2017.

He topped out in the Seattle system at Triple-A, and the Mariners dealt him to San Diego, where he saw his first major-league action in 2022. The Padres sent him to Atlanta in December 2023, but Tommy John surgery sidelined him for much of 2024 and all of 2025. After a stint playing for Atlanta's Triple-A Gwinnett Stripers, he returned to Atlanta's roster in August, and here we are.

Weiss told Kerr on Wednesday that he'd be starting the critical Game 3, though the game's actual start time remained very much in question, because of MLB's scheduling shenanigans.

"It was kind of hectic because we didn't know if the game was starting at 2 or 8," Kerr said after the game, drenched in celebratory Champagne. "So I was like, 'Am I going to bed this time, or this time?'"

Kerr settled his mind the best way he knew how: with a viewing of Druski's horror comedy "Livestream from Hell." On Thursday, with the rest of the clubhouse staying loose by talking about their fantasy football teams, he stayed locked in, focusing on the culmination of a dream he'd carried for his entire life.

Kerr faced the teeth of Philadelphia's order right from the start. In the first inning, he surrendered only a single to Kyle Schwarber while inducing outs from Trea Turner and Alec Bohm and striking out the mighty and dreaded Bryce Harper. Given a three-run cushion in the bottom of the first, he cruised from there, facing the minimum until the top of the fourth, when a walk to Schwarber and a forceout of Harper brought Weiss to the mound to wrap up Kerr's night.

"He wasn't rattled at all," Weiss said. "Looked like a 10-year vet making a start, and he was phenomenal."

Still, this is Atlanta, land of 28-3, home of the one-World-Series-in-the-'90s Braves, where nobody's too comfortable until a good five or six months after winning a trophy. So yes, the Braves posted a 3-0 lead in the bottom of the first on Michael Harris II's three-run shot, and yes, Atlanta added two more runs in the fourth off Ozzie Albies' bat, and yes, Matt Olson added a sixth in the seventh. But when Philadelphia's Derek Hill tripled to start the eighth, and Turner sacrificed him home, and Schwarber and Harper lurked, well, it didn't matter that the Phillies' win probability was a mere 2.3%. A murmur ran through the Truist Park crowd. If it could happen to anyone …

So Sale came on to finish the eighth and pitch the ninth. But to get there, we have to take a detour through Weiss' office.

Weiss arrived at the ballpark on Thursday to find Sale sitting in his office, grinning.

"I feel amazing," Sale said, despite the fact that he'd thrown 6 ⅓ innings of playoff ball just two days prior.

Weiss had already decided not to ask Sale if he wanted to pitch, since he knew Sale would say yes, even if his arm were hanging on by a thread. But when Sale made the offer, Weiss happily took him up on it. They mapped out a plan to have Sale face the wicked top of Philadelphia's order late in the game, and that's exactly how it played out, with Sale blowing away Harper in the bottom of the eighth and striking out two more to close out the ninth.

"I've run out of superlatives for Chris Sale," Weiss said. "When you take everything into consideration — teammate, competitor, performer, work ethic, all those things — he's as good as I've ever been around."

Coming from a guy who has played baseball alongside and against the best of the past four decades, that's some high praise.

It's impossible to overstate the psychological lift this series win will have on both Braves players and Braves fans. This is a team that has played consistently strong, often excellent baseball for more than 35 years, with only two World Series rings to show for it. That's the same as the Marlins and Blue Jays, just one more than the Royals, Nationals and Angels.

Over the past 27 seasons dating to 2000, the Braves have reached the playoffs 16 times. But in that entire stretch, they've won their initial series just four times, including this year. And they've won multiple playoff series in a single postseason just twice, in 2020 and in 2021, their world championship year.

Now, though, the win-loss record resets to 0-0. The Braves travel to Los Angeles to take on the Dodgers, a team Atlanta beat five out of six times in the regular season. There's still October baseball ahead for these Braves, as unexpected as that might've seemed at the start of this year.

"Nobody had us making the playoffs," Weiss said. "These guys have overcome so much. Then to boot, at the end of the year, we lose three more starters. We barely have enough starters to play a series, yet it's guys like Ray Kerr and everybody else that step up and perform when the stakes are highest. It's such a great group."

The Braves begin the NLDS against the Dodgers on Saturday in Los Angeles and will return to Atlanta for at least one game starting Tuesday. Who will pitch? Who's to say? The Braves probably won't want to attempt the same sort of all-hands-on-deck strategy they employed in Game 3, but they now know for sure that it's an option.

articles.title: MLB World Series 2026 Odds for Updated Playoffs Bracket Entering ALDS, NLDS
articles.summary: What was once—ostensibly at least—a 30-team race to the 2026 World Series title has been whittled down to eight.
articles.body:
What was once—ostensibly at least—a 30-team race to the 2026 World Series title has been whittled down to eight.

All four matchups for the divisonal round are now set after the Atlanta Braves eliminted the Philadelphia Phillies with a 6-2 triumph Thursday night.

While there are arguments to be made on behalf of all eight teams—from the team-of-destiny underdog Chicago White Sox to the absurdly stacked Los Angeles Dodgers—oddsmakers understandably (and rightfully) see some separation in this field.

We'll dig into those differences with a latest look at the World Series odds, courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook , before spotlighting three teams from different tiers of the hierarchy.

The Favorite: Los Angeles Dodgers (+230)

The baseball world hasn't seen a run of three consecutive World Series wins since the Yankees went back-to-back-to-back in 1998-2000. The Dodgers have a chance to end that drought.

Their path to glory this time around could look a lot like the last two: following the lead of their stars and getting timely contributions from their support players. Shohei Ohtani is a game-breaker of the highest order (even if he isn't pitching), Andy Pages just announced his arrival as a star and the accolades attached to Freddie Freeman, Mookie Betts and Kyle Tucker are too numerous to mention.

As loaded as the lineup still looks, the rotation shines even brighter. Between Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tyler Glasnow and Blake Snell, L.A. boasts a ferocious foursome that is simply unrivaled across the league. The bullpen can be leaky, and the offensive stars haven't all shined as bright as normal, but with elite starting pitching like this, that may not even matter.

Despite securing the AL's top seed and the home-field advantage that comes along with it, Tampa sits just fourth among World Series-hopefuls.

Skepticism from the oddsmakers isn't totally unwarranted, though. The Rays aren't exactly an offensive powerhouse, and their rotation is without Shane McClanahan (forearm tightness).

That said, Tampa secured this spot with great bat-to-ball contact, chaos on the basepath, reliable defense and quality pitching from the rotation to the bullpen. The Rays have had a great season, so they have to look tempting with less-than-top-dollar odds.
